api.base_url: https://v3.football.api-sports.io/ (direct API-SPORTS account; docs v3.9.3 state literally "API-SPORTS : https://v3.football.api-sports.io/"). Endpoints append directly, e.g. https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures and https://v3.football.api-sports.io/status. RapidAPI resellers use a DIFFERENT host: https://api-football-v1.p.rapidapi.com/v3/ (note the extra /v3 path segment). NOTE: the current official documentation page no longer documents the RapidAPI variant at all — the RapidAPI host/prefix is confirmed only from the RapidAPI marketplace listing and third-party sources, not from api-football.com today.
api.auth:
DIRECT api-sports.io account: send the key in the request header `x-apisports-key: <YOUR_KEY>` (lowercase, exactly as documented). No `x-rapidapi-host` and no Bearer/Authorization header.

CRITICAL, quoted from the docs: "The API is configured to work only with GET requests and allows only the headers listed below: x-apisports-key. If you make non-GET requests or add headers that are not in the list, you will receive an error from the API." It further warns: "Some frameworks (especially in JS, nodeJS..) automatically add extra headers, you have to make sure to remove them in order to get a response from the API." So strip default Content-Type/Accept-Encoding/User-Agent-style extras your HTTP client injects if you get unexplained errors.

RAPIDAPI account (different product, different key): base https://api-football-v1.p.rapidapi.com/v3/ with TWO headers — `x-rapidapi-key: <YOUR_RAPIDAPI_KEY>` and `x-rapidapi-host: api-football-v1.p.rapidapi.com`. The two key types are NOT interchangeable: an api-sports.io key will not work against the RapidAPI host and vice versa. Response bodies are otherwise identical.

curl example (direct):
curl -s "https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=39&season=2024" -H "x-apisports-key: XxXxXxXxXxXxXxXxXxXxXxXx"

Free self-check endpoint: GET https://v3.football.api-sports.io/status — docs state "This call does not count against the daily quota." It returns response.subscription.plan, response.subscription.end, response.subscription.active, response.requests.current and response.requests.limit_day. Use it as your sync's preflight/health check for free.
api.free_tier_limits:
CONFIRMED from api-football.com/pricing (read today): Free plan = $0/month, "100 Requests / day".

CONFIRMED from the official "HOW RATELIMIT WORKS" post (dated June 12, 2026): per-minute limits by plan — "Free plan: 10 requests per minute. Pro plan: 300 requests per minute or 5 requests per second. Ultra plan: 450 requests per minute or 7 requests per second. Mega plan: 900 requests per minute or 15 requests per second. Custom plan: 1200 requests per minute or 20 requests per second."

So free tier = 100 req/day, 10 req/min. All endpoints are available on Free — the pricing page says "All our plans include all competitions and endpoints."

SEASON RESTRICTION (real, but exact range NOT published): the pricing page says only "(Free plans are limited in terms of available seasons)" and the official beginner's guide says "The difference between plans is purely about volume and historical range, not features. Paid plans unlock deeper historical archives. The free plan covers recent seasons." NEITHER page names the specific seasons. I could NOT confirm the commonly-repeated "free = seasons 2021-2023" claim from any official page. Verify empirically with your own key: call /leagues?id=39 and read response[0].seasons[] — the seasons your key can actually query are the ones returned there. Requesting a season outside your plan returns an errors payload rather than data.

Quota reset: not stated on the pages I read. Widely reported as midnight UTC; treat as UNCONFIRMED and instead trust the `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining` response header as ground truth.

Overage behaviour (confirmed from the ratelimit post): there is a burst/queue layer — requests slightly over the per-minute rate are "temporarily paused and then executed as soon as the traffic goes back under the threshold", but beyond that "the API returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests" error. Note 429 is NOT listed in the endpoint's documented response codes (which list only 200/204/499/500), so handle it explicitly.

Also confirmed: image/logo URLs on media.api-sports.io "do not count towards your daily quota and are provided for free" but are separately rate-limited per second/minute.
api.fixtures_endpoint:
WHOLE SEASON FOR ONE LEAGUE IN ONE CALL (this is the documented use case "Get all available fixtures from one {league} & {season}"):

  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=39&season=2024

That single call returns every fixture of the season — the official tutorial confirms the England Premier League league=39 season=2024 is "20 teams, giving a total of 380 matches spread over 38 rounds" and retrieves them without paging. 1 request = 1 quota unit for the entire season. `season` is the 4-digit STARTING year (2024 == the 2024/25 campaign).

Add a timezone so kickoff strings come back in your local zone:
  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=39&season=2024&timezone=Europe/London

DATE RANGE (documented example verbatim from the docs' "Use Cases" panel):
  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=61&season=2019&from=2019-07-01&to=2020-10-31&timezone=Europe/London
and the team-scoped variant:
  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?team=85&season=2019&from=2019-07-01&to=2020-10-31

Both `from` and `to` are `YYYY-MM-DD`. IMPORTANT: every official from/to example also passes `season` together with `league` or `team` — I could NOT confirm whether bare `?from=...&to=...` works alone. Assume from/to must be scoped by league+season or team+season and always send them.

SINGLE DAY:  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?date=2019-10-22
DAY + LEAGUE: https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?date=2020-01-30&league=61&season=2019
NEXT/LAST N:  https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?next=15   |  ?last=15  |  ?league=61&next=10  |  ?venue=358&next=10
STATUS FILTER (dash-separated, confirmed by the official tutorial): https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=39&season=2024&status=FT-AET-PEN  (the tutorial adds 1H-HT-2H-ET-BT-P for in-progress). Case-insensitive — a docs example uses lowercase `status=ft`.
BY ROUND:    https://v3.football.api-sports.io/fixtures?league=61&season=2019&round=Regular Season - 1  (URL-encode the round string)
BY ID(S):    ?id=215662  or  ?ids=215662-215663-215664  (max 20 ids)
LIVE:        ?live=all  or  ?live=39-61-48

Note: requesting a single fixture via `?id=` returns events, lineups, statistics and player stats embedded in the response; the bulk league/season call does NOT include those.
query_params: id (integer) — a single fixture id. Returns the fixture WITH embedded events, lineups, statistics and players.
ids (string, 'id-id-id') — several fixture ids, dash-separated. HARD CAP: 'Maximum of 20 fixtures ids' per call. Also returns embedded events/lineups/statistics/players.
live (string, 'all' or 'id-id') — all in-play fixtures, or in-play filtered to several LEAGUE ids. Embeds events in the response.
date (string, YYYY-MM-DD) — all fixtures on one calendar date.
league (integer) — league id (e.g. 39 = Premier League, 61 = Ligue 1).
season (integer, exactly 4 chars YYYY) — the season's STARTING year; 2024 means 2024/25. Required alongside league to pull a full season.
last (integer, <= 2 characters, so max 99) — the X most recent fixtures.
next (integer, <= 2 characters, so max 99) — the X upcoming fixtures. Best cheap daily-sync probe for a league: ?league=61&next=10
from (string, YYYY-MM-DD) — range start. Always pair with season + (league|team) as in every official example.
round (string) — matchday label, e.g. 'Regular Season - 1'. Must exactly match a value returned by GET /fixtures/rounds?league=X&season=Y. URL-encode it (contains spaces and a hyphen).
status (string) — one or more status SHORT codes, dash-separated, e.g. status=NS or status=NS-PST-FT or status=FT-AET-PEN. Case-insensitive.
timezone (string) — an IANA zone name, e.g. 'Europe/London'. Must be a value from GET /timezone. Default is UTC.
page — NOT a valid parameter on /fixtures. It exists only on a handful of other endpoints (players, odds, etc.) where the docs say 'Use for the pagination' with Default: 1.
status_codes: TBD — long: 'Time To Be Defined' — type: Scheduled — 'Scheduled but date and time are not known'. Treat fixture.date as a PLACEHOLDER, not a real kickoff.
NS — long: 'Not Started' — type: Scheduled — (docs give no extra description). The normal pre-match state.
1H — long: 'First Half, Kick Off' — type: In Play — 'First half in play'
HT — long: 'Halftime' — type: In Play — docs description reads 'Finished in the regular time' (this is a copy/paste error in the official table; HT means half time)
2H — long: 'Second Half, 2nd Half Started' — type: In Play — 'Second half in play'
ET — long: 'Extra Time' — type: In Play — 'Extra time in play'
BT — long: 'Break Time' — type: In Play — 'Break during extra time'
P — long: 'Penalty In Progress' — type: In Play — 'Penaly played after extra time' (sic, typo is in the official docs)
SUSP — long: 'Match Suspended' — type: In Play — "Suspended by referee's decision, may be rescheduled another day"
INT — long: 'Match Interrupted' — type: In Play — "Interrupted by referee's decision, should resume in a few minutes"
FT — long: 'Match Finished' — type: Finished — 'Finished in the regular time'
AET — long: 'Match Finished' — type: Finished — 'Finished after extra time without going to the penalty shootout'
PEN — long: 'Match Finished' — type: Finished — 'Finished after the penalty shootout'
PST — long: 'Match Postponed' — type: Postponed — 'Postponed to another day, once the new date and time is known the status will change to Not Started'
CANC — long: 'Match Cancelled' — type: Cancelled — 'Cancelled, match will not be played'

ABD — long: 'Match Abandoned' — type: Abandoned — 'Abandoned for various reasons (Bad Weather, Safety, Floodlights, Playing Staff Or Referees), Can be rescheduled or not, it depends on the competition'
AWD — long: 'Technical Loss' — type: Not Played — (docs give no extra description)
WO — long: 'WalkOver' — type: Not Played — 'Victory by forfeit or absence of competitor'
LIVE — long: 'In Progress' — type: In Play — 'Used in very rare cases. It indicates a fixture in progress but the data indicating the half-time or elapsed time are not available'
api.reschedule_detection:
CONFIRMED, and this is the single most important sentence in the docs for your use case: "The fixtures ids are unique and specific to each fixture. In no case an ID will change."

So a rescheduled match KEEPS its fixture.id and gets a NEW fixture.date / fixture.timestamp in place. It is an UPDATE, never a delete+insert.

The documented lifecycle for a postponement, quoted: PST = "Postponed to another day, once the new date and time is known the status will change to Not Started." So the transition you diff for is:
  (id=X, status=PST, date=D1)  ->  (id=X, status=NS, date=D2)
A match can also go straight NS(D1) -> NS(D2) if the reschedule is announced without ever passing through PST, and TBD -> NS once a provisional date firms up. Docs: "Fixtures with the status TBD may indicate an incorrect fixture date or time because the fixture date or time is not yet known or final. Fixtures with this status are checked and updated daily. The same applies to fixtures with the status PST, CANC."

THERE IS NO LAST-UPDATED / updated_at / modified FIELD. I inspected the fully expanded official /fixtures response sample field by field and the complete query-parameter list: the only time-like fields are fixture.date (kickoff), fixture.timestamp (kickoff, Unix), and fixture.periods.first / fixture.periods.second (period kickoff epochs). There is no change-feed, no webhook, no If-Modified-Since support, and no ?updated_since parameter. Confirmed absent, not merely unfound.

THEREFORE the daily diff must be client-side, keyed on fixture.id:
1. Once per day pull the whole season per league in ONE call: GET /fixtures?league=39&season=2024&timezone=UTC (1 quota unit).
2. Upsert into a local table keyed by fixture.id, storing at minimum: timestamp (int), status_short, round, venue.id, teams.home.id, teams.away.id, plus a content hash of those fields and your own synced_at.
3. Compute the delta against the previous snapshot:
   - id present before and now, and new.timestamp != old.timestamp  => MOVED. Report "moved from old.timestamp to new.timestamp".
   - old.status_short == 'PST' and new.status_short == 'NS'          => reschedule confirmed with a firm date.
   - old.status_short == 'NS' and new.status_short == 'PST'          => newly postponed, new date not yet known (fixture.date will still show the OLD slot until the API firms it up — do not trust it).
   - new.status_short in ('CANC','ABD','AWD','WO')                    => will not be played / not played normally; stop tracking for a fixture date.
   - new.status_short == 'TBD'                                        => date is provisional; suppress it from any user-facing calendar or flag it clearly.
   - id present before, absent now                                    => rare, but treat as withdrawn/removed rather than assuming a new id appeared.
   - id absent before, present now                                    => newly added fixture (common for cup rounds once the draw is made).
4. Compare on fixture.timestamp (integer epoch), NOT on the fixture.date string — the string carries whatever timezone you requested, so a change in your `timezone` parameter would otherwise look like every match moved. Always sync with timezone=UTC and convert for display.

Cost: one call per league per day. On the free tier's 100/day you can diff roughly 90 leagues daily with headroom, or the same league far more often.
api.response_shape:
Every response uses the same envelope (top level):
  get            -> string, the endpoint called, e.g. "fixtures"
  parameters     -> object echoing your query params, e.g. {"live": "all"}
  errors         -> [] when fine (see gotchas — it becomes a populated object on failure)
  results        -> integer, number of items in response[]
  paging         -> {"current": 1, "total": 1}
  response       -> array of fixture objects

Per element of response[] (exact paths, from the official expanded sample):

FIXTURE BLOCK
  response[i].fixture.id                  -> integer, e.g. 239625. STABLE FOREVER. Your primary key.
  response[i].fixture.referee             -> string|null, e.g. null
  response[i].fixture.timezone            -> string, e.g. "UTC" — echoes the timezone the dates are rendered in
  response[i].fixture.date                -> ISO-8601 string WITH offset, e.g. "2020-02-06T14:00:00+00:00"
  response[i].fixture.timestamp           -> integer Unix epoch seconds, e.g. 1580997600. TIMEZONE-INDEPENDENT — diff on this.
  response[i].fixture.periods.first       -> integer|null epoch of 1st-half kickoff, e.g. 1580997600
  response[i].fixture.periods.second      -> integer|null epoch of 2nd-half kickoff, e.g. null
  response[i].fixture.venue.id            -> integer|null, e.g. 1887
  response[i].fixture.venue.name          -> string|null, e.g. "Stade Municipal"
  response[i].fixture.venue.city          -> string|null, e.g. "Oued Zem"
  response[i].fixture.status.long         -> string, e.g. "Halftime"
  response[i].fixture.status.short        -> string, e.g. "HT" — the code to switch on
  response[i].fixture.status.elapsed      -> integer|null minutes played, e.g. 45
  response[i].fixture.status.extra        -> integer|null — added time in the half. NEW in 3.9.3.

LEAGUE BLOCK
  response[i].league.id                   -> integer, e.g. 200
  response[i].league.name                 -> string, e.g. "Botola Pro"
  response[i].league.country              -> string, e.g. "Morocco"
  response[i].league.logo                 -> URL string, e.g. "https://media.api-sports.io/football/leagues/115.png"
  response[i].league.flag                 -> URL string|null, e.g. "https://media.api-sports.io/flags/ma.svg"
  response[i].league.season               -> integer, e.g. 2019
  response[i].league.round                -> string ROUND/MATCHDAY LABEL, e.g. "Regular Season - 14". Free text, NOT an integer — for cups it reads like "Quarter-finals", "Group Stage - 3". Parse the trailing number only after confirming the prefix.
  response[i].league.standings            -> boolean, whether the competition covers standings. NEW in 3.9.3 and MISSING from the docs' own sample JSON — expect it at runtime.

TEAMS BLOCK
  response[i].teams.home.id               -> integer, e.g. 967
  response[i].teams.home.name             -> string, e.g. "Rapide Oued ZEM"
  response[i].teams.home.logo             -> URL string, e.g. "https://media.api-sports.io/football/teams/967.png"
  response[i].teams.home.winner           -> boolean|null (null while undecided/drawn), e.g. false
  response[i].teams.away.id / .name / .logo / .winner  -> same shape, e.g. 968 / "Wydad AC" / "https://media.api-sports.io/football/teams/968.png" / true

GOALS (current/final score)
  response[i].goals.home                  -> integer|null, e.g. 0
  response[i].goals.away                  -> integer|null, e.g. 1

SCORE BREAKDOWN (each is {home, away}, integers or null)
  response[i].score.halftime.home / .away   -> e.g. 0 / 1
  response[i].score.fulltime.home / .away   -> null until FT
  response[i].score.extratime.home / .away  -> null unless ET played
  response[i].score.penalty.home / .away    -> null unless shootout

TIMEZONE HANDLING: default is UTC. Pass ?timezone=Europe/London to have fixture.date and fixture.timezone rendered in that zone; the value must come from GET /timezone (docs: "To know the list of available time zones you have to use the endpoint timezone"). fixture.timestamp is the absolute instant and is the field to persist and compare. Whether the `date`/`from`/`to` FILTERS are evaluated in the requested timezone or in UTC is NOT stated in the docs — I could not confirm it; sync with timezone=UTC and widen ranges by a day at the edges to be safe.
api.pagination:
/fixtures is effectively NOT paginated. `page` is not among its documented query parameters, and the official tutorial pulls all 380 Premier League fixtures for league=39&season=2024 in a single call. Expect paging.total == 1 and the full result set in response[]. The envelope still always carries the paging object: "paging": { "current": 1, "total": 1 } Defensive client code should still read paging.total and loop `for p in 2..paging.total` appending &page=

— it costs nothing and protects you if the provider ever shards large season pulls. But do not build the sync assuming paging is required. Pagination is real on OTHER endpoints only: a `page` parameter documented as "integer, Default: 1, Use for the pagination" appears on 4 endpoints (players, odds and similar). If you later add player or odds sync, each extra page is a separate quota unit — which matters a lot on 100 requests/day. Use `results` (integer) as the count of items actually returned; a query that matches nothing returns HTTP 204 No Content (documented) rather than a 200 with an empty array, so your client must handle an empty body without trying to JSON-parse it.
gotchas: HTTP 200 does NOT mean success. The documented response codes for /fixtures are only 200 OK, 204 No Content, 499 Time Out and 500 Internal Server Error — there is no documented 4xx for a bad parameter or an out-of-plan season. The API signals those inside the body via the top-level `errors` member. ALWAYS check `errors` before trusting `response`. Widely observed (not stated in the docs, so verify with your key): `errors` is an empty ARRAY `[]` on success but a populated OBJECT/dict on failure — that type flip breaks strictly-typed deserializers in Go, Rust, Java and Pydantic. Model it as a permissive union.

204 No Content is returned for empty result sets. Do not call .json() on the body unconditionally — check the status code first or you will throw on an empty payload during quiet parts of the calendar.

429 Too Many Requests is real but UNDOCUMENTED in the endpoint's response-code list. The rate-limit article confirms 'the API returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests error' once the burst queue can no longer absorb your rate. On Free that is 10 req/min. Implement exponential backoff with jitter and honour X-RateLimit-Remaining.

There are FOUR rate-limit headers with INCONSISTENT casing — two lowercase daily ones and two capitalised per-minute ones: `x-ratelimit-requests-limit` (per day), `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining` (per day), `X-RateLimit-Limit` (per minute), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (per minute). Read them case-insensitively; do not confuse the daily pair with the per-minute pair.

Adding ANY header beyond x-apisports-key can make the request fail. Docs: the API 'allows only the headers listed below: x-apisports-key' and warns that JS/NodeJS frameworks 'automatically add extra headers, you have to make sure to remove them'. Only GET is accepted. If you get inexplicable errors, dump and strip your client's default headers first.

Do NOT run the sync from shared-IP serverless. The official rate-limit post explicitly names Cloudflare Workers, AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Run, Google Cloud Functions, Firebase Functions, Vercel Functions and Netlify Functions, warning that limits also apply per IP so 'another user on the same IP' can trigger protections against you, and recommends 'a dedicated static IP'. It also warns access 'may be temporarily or permanently blocked by our firewall without prior notice'.

fixture.date is a rendered string in whatever timezone you asked for; fixture.timestamp is the absolute epoch. Persist and diff on `timestamp`. If you diff on the date string and someone changes the `timezone` parameter, every fixture in the league will look rescheduled at once.

TBD fixtures carry a FAKE date. Docs: 'Fixtures with the status TBD may indicate an incorrect fixture date or time because the fixture date or time is not yet known or final.' Never surface a TBD kickoff as confirmed, and never alert on TBD date churn — it will flap daily.

A newly-postponed match keeps its OLD date while status flips to PST. The new date only appears later, when status flips back to NS. So PST -> NS is your 'reschedule confirmed' signal; NS -> PST is only 'this is not happening as planned'.

There is no updated_at field, no change feed, no webhooks and no If-Modified-Since. Every reschedule detection must be a client-side snapshot diff keyed on fixture.id. Budget storage for yesterday's snapshot, not just today's.

league.round is a free-text label ('Regular Season - 14', 'Quarter-finals', 'Group Stage - 3'), not an integer, and it is what the ?round= filter must match EXACTLY — fetch valid values from GET /fixtures/rounds?league=X&season=Y and URL-encode them (they contain spaces and hyphens).
`season` is the STARTING year: 2024 = the 2024/25 season. Getting this off by one silently returns the wrong campaign rather than an error.

The Free plan restricts which seasons you can query, but neither the pricing page nor the docs names them — the pricing page only says '(Free plans are limited in terms of available seasons)'. Discover your real range from /leagues?id=<X> -> response[0].seasons[] rather than hardcoding. The frequently-repeated '2021-2023' figure is NOT officially confirmed anywhere I could find.

The docs' own /fixtures response sample is STALE: changelog 3.9.3 adds `fixture.status.extra` and `league.standings`, and `league.standings` does not appear in the printed sample. Do not generate a strict schema from the sample alone — allow unknown fields.

status.short values are not unique per long name: FT, AET and PEN all have long name 'Match Finished'. Switch on `short`, never on `long`. Also note ABD (Abandoned) is a distinct terminal-ish state that 'can be rescheduled or not, it depends on the competition' — you must keep polling abandoned fixtures.

Not every competition has livescore. Docs: 'the status remains in NS and will be updated in the minutes/hours following the match (this can take up to 48 hours, depending on the competition).' So a fixture stuck at NS well past its kickoff is normal for minor competitions and must not be treated as an anomaly or a reschedule.
?ids= accepts a MAXIMUM of 20 fixture ids per call; `next` and `last` are capped at '2 characters', i.e. 99. Chunk accordingly.

Fetching by ?id= or ?ids= returns a much heavier payload (events, lineups, statistics and player stats embedded) than the bulk league/season call. For a daily fixture sync always use the league+season form — it is one quota unit and a far smaller body.
GET /status does not count against the daily quota — use it freely for preflight, plan checks and alerting on quota exhaustion instead of burning a real call.

Logo/flag URLs on media.api-sports.io are free of daily quota but separately rate-limited per second/minute; the docs recommend caching them your side or fronting them with a CDN. Do not hotlink them from a high-traffic page.

api-football.com sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge, so the DOCS are not scrapable by plain HTTP clients (403). The API host v3.football.api-sports.io is unaffected — do not confuse a docs-fetch failure with an API outage.

Recommended call frequency from the docs: '1 call per minute for the leagues, teams, fixtures who have at least one fixture in progress otherwise 1 call per day.' The /fixtures data itself refreshes every 15 seconds, but polling faster than the guidance on Free will exhaust 100 requests within roughly 100 minutes.

ids.season_param:
Pass **season=2026** for the 2026/27 European season.

CONFIRMED: api-football v3 numbers every split-year season by its STARTING year, and the parameter is documented as `integer = 4 characters YYYY` (verbatim from the live docs at https://www.api-football.com/documentation-v3, QUERY PARAMETERS block for /leagues, /fixtures, /standings).

Evidence for the start-year convention (all from a real `/leagues` dump in github.com/yorobot/sport.db.more/api-football/LEAGUES.md + LEAGUES.WORLD.md, which prints "(id) Type, Country | Name -- (n): <season list>"):
- (39) England | Premier League -- 15 seasons: 2010...2024. 2010/11 through 2024/25 is exactly 15 seasons, so label 2024 = the 2024/25 campaign.
- (48) England | League Cup -- 14 seasons: 2011...2024 = 2011/12 ... 2024/25. Consistent.
- (2) UEFA Champions League -- 2011...2024, i.e. label 2024 = the 2024/25 edition (final June 2025).
- (556) Spain | Super Cup -- 9 seasons: 2016...2024. There have been exactly 9 Supercopa editions from Aug 2016 to Jan 2025 (Aug'16, Aug'17, Aug'18, Jan'20, Jan'21, Jan'22, Jan'23, Jan'24, Jan'25). The one-to-one mapping means the January-played editions are labelled by the STARTING year of the surrounding season (Jan 2025 edition = season 2024). Important consequence: the Supercopa played in January 2027 must be requested as season=2026, NOT 2027. Same logic for Copa del Rey and the FA/EFL Cup finals played in spring 2027 — all season=2026.
- Independent code confirmation: FootyUpdateHQ/footyupdateshq-website/src/lib/api-football/season.ts — `getActiveSeasonStartYear()` returns `month >= 8 ? year : year - 1` with the comment "Uses the season start year (e.g. 2025 for the 2025/26 campaign)"; and gaborbencsik/tipp-game/plans/api-football-ids.md (dated 2026-04-29) validating World Cup 2026 with `season=2026`.

Caveat: single-calendar-year competitions (World Cup, Euros, Copa America, Club World Cup, most South American/Scandinavian leagues) are labelled by their calendar year instead — but none of your nine are in that group. All nine of yours are split-year and take 2026.

ids.free_plan_coverage:
SHOWSTOPPER: **No. The FREE plan cannot serve season=2026.** It is currently restricted to seasons 2022, 2023 and 2024.

Official statement (read live off https://www.api-football.com/pricing today, 2026-08-19, via browser since the site 403s scrapers): "All our plans include all competitions and endpoints." followed immediately by the parenthetical "(Free plans are limited in terms of available seasons)". So the LEAGUE coverage is fine — all nine of your competitions are in every plan, including free. The restriction is purely the SEASON axis, and it is enforced server-side.

Exact error string, from two independent live tests:
- github.com/NareshKoirala/fpl-oracle/debug/research/api-football.md shows a raw response body for `GET /leagues?name=premier league&season=2025`: `"errors":{"plan":"Free plans do not have access to this season, try from 2022 to 2024."}, "results":0, "response":[]` — note it returns HTTP 200 with an empty array, so naive code silently gets zero rows rather than an exception.
- github.com/gaborbencsik/tipp-game/plans/api-football-ids.md, dated 2026-04-29, from a POC script run against a live free key: "A Free tier (100 req/nap) csak 2022-2024 szezonokhoz ad hozzaferest. Aktualis szezon (2025, 2026) -> Pro ($19/ho) szukseges." with the same quoted error message.

The window rolls forward but lags ~2 seasons: an earlier live test (github.com/Tiniqua/PerfResearch/docs/archive/API_FOOTBALL_INVESTIGATION.md, dated 2025-11-29) recorded "try from 2021 to 2023". By 2026-04 it had advanced to 2022-2024. It has NOT reached 2026 and will not for roughly two more years. Also corroborated by github.com/FootyUpdateHQ/footyupdateshq-website/src/lib/api-football/season.ts: `export const FREE_PLAN_MAX_SEASON = 2024;`.

WHAT STILL WORKS ON FREE for current 2026/27 data (all live-verified in the sources above, useful if you want to avoid paying):
1. `GET /fixtures?date=YYYY-MM-DD` with NO league/season params — works, returns all current-season fixtures worldwide for that date including finished scores. BUT the date must be inside a ~3-day rolling window [today-1, today+1] UTC; outside it you get "Free plans do not have access to this date, try from <today-1> to <today+1>." (confirmed still in force across API-SPORTS in Aug 2026 by github.com/Ozaveshe/oddspadi/docs/fixture-reconciliation.md, which quotes the window "2026-08-06 to 2026-08-08"). You then have to filter to your nine league ids client-side.
2. `GET /fixtures?live=all` — works, returns in-play current-season matches.
3. `GET /fixtures?id=<fixture_id>` — single-fixture lookup is explicitly EXEMPT from the current-season block (documented in github.com/10urok10/FootballPrediction/CLAUDE.md: "unlike bulk league+season queries" it is "exempt from the 'no current season on free plan' block").
4. `GET /odds?date=` — same ~1-day window restriction.

WHAT DOES NOT WORK ON FREE: any bulk `league=<id>&season=2026` call. That kills full-season fixture lists, standings, top scorers, team season statistics, `last`/`next` fixture params, and any historical backfill for 2025/26 or 2026/27. At 100 requests/day you also cannot brute-force it via daily date polling for long.

RECOMMENDATION: for a 2026/27 project the free plan is not viable as the primary source. The Pro plan is $19/month (7,500 req/day) and lifts the season restriction — that is the cheapest fix. Alternatives if the budget is zero: football-data.org free tier (covers PL, La Liga, UCL current season, but NOT the domestic cups — no FA Cup/EFL Cup/Copa del Rey/Supercopa), or TheSportsDB (keyless test key "123", covers cups, lower data quality). A hybrid — free api-football on the date/live/id endpoints polled daily, cached into your own store — is technically possible but fragile and cannot backfill history.

I did **not** rely on the yorobot dump the claim leans on (that is one source, re-cited five times). I also re-downloaded and grepped the yorobot dumps myself rather than trusting the quoted lines (`.../scratchpad/LEAGUES.md`, `LEAGUES.WORLD.md`) — the quoted lines are accurate, verbatim.

Two sources I found myself, neither cited in the claim:

Extracting the ranges: **53 × "try from 2022 to 2024"**, **12 × "try from 2021 to 2023"** (the older, pre-2026 window). **Zero** occurrences of any range containing 2025 or 2026. Files quoting 2022–2024 are committed continuously through 2026-08-18.

It is enforced server-side, returns **HTTP 200** with `"results":0, "response":[]` plus an `errors.plan` object — so naive code gets zero rows, not an exception. **League coverage is fine** — the restriction is purely the season axis. Live pricing page today: "All our plans include all competitions and endpoints." with the parenthetical "(Free plans are limited in terms of available seasons)".

## 2. Live pricing, read off https://www.api-football.com/pricing today (2026-08-19)

| Plan | Price | Req/day | Req/min |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | 100 | 10 |

Net: on Free you can only ever see fixtures for yesterday/today/tomorrow, cannot filter them by league server-side, and cannot backfill or look ahead at all. **That is fatal for a fixture calendar.** At 100 req/day you also cannot brute-force it.

## 4. Corrections to the two claims

**Claim 1 — three flaws, none load-bearing:**
- The `Ozaveshe/oddspadi` citation for the date window is **misattributed**: that table row is **api-basketball (Free)**, not api-football. The window is nonetheless real for api-football (independently confirmed by `slavik03-png/-ai-stavki/.agents/memory/api-football-free-plan-limits.md`, 2026-07-15, and `10urok10/FootballPrediction/CLAUDE.md` for `/odds?date=`).
- "will not reach 2026 for roughly two more years" is **extrapolation, not evidence**. Two datapoints (2021-2023 → 2022-2024) do not establish a rate. Treat as unknown.
- It omits that `next`/`last` are blocked with their *own* distinct error, and that `league`+`date` is blocked because `season` becomes mandatory.

**Claim 2 — the numbers are right, the advice is wrong.** Its recommendation — *"call /leagues?id=39 and read response[0].seasons[] — the seasons your key can actually query are the ones returned there"* — is **empirically false in both directions**, per Madooo's live tests:

- False negative: 2026 is flagged `coverage=false` yet fetches perfectly on Pro (380 fixtures, ten days before kickoff). Filtering on coverage would hide the exact season you want.

Its caution that no official page names the seasons is correct — but the range **is** empirically established (2022–2024), so "UNCONFIRMED" understates it. Also note the official beginner's guide (March 13 2026) is actively misleading here: *"Paid plans unlock deeper historical archives. The free plan covers recent seasons."* The truth is the inverse — free gets a frozen mid-window and is denied the **current** season.

Minor: claim 2 says 429 isn't in the documented response codes; the beginner's guide does document it ("429 is a request blocked by ratelimit"). Quota reset time remains unverified — api-sports.io/faq is behind a Cloudflare bot challenge I did not bypass; trust `x-ratelimit-requests-remaining` instead. Madooo also warns that counter is **not monotonic** (observed 77, 75, 78, 76 in one run).

## 5. Recommendation

For a 2026/27 calendar across leagues 39, 45, 48, 140, 143, 556, 2, 3, 848: **the free plan is not viable, full stop.** Budget **$19/month for Pro** (or ~$13.30/mo equivalent on the discounted long prepay). At 9 competitions × 1 call/day that is ~9 of 7,500 requests — Pro is enormous overkill for this workload, but it is the cheapest tier that lifts the season block.

Zero-budget alternatives, both with real gaps: football-data.org free tier covers PL/La Liga/UCL current season but **not the domestic cups** (no FA Cup, EFL Cup, Copa del Rey, Supercopa), and TheSportsDB (keyless test key `123`) covers cups at lower data quality — that is what `10urok10/FootballPrediction` switched to precisely because "its free plan cannot query the current/upcoming season for *fixtures*".
